correctness.rationale: Zapletal's Theorem 1.1 gives, relative to Con(ZFC), a model of ZF+DC+BPI with no E0 selector. Larson--Zapletal Observation 3.13 proves in ZF+DC that a Hamel basis of R over Q yields a total E0 selector. The source model satisfies DC, so the latter implication applies internally; because its conclusion fails, no Hamel basis exists there. BPI implies Hahn--Banach, yielding the stated Hahn--Banach corollary.

value.rationale: The statement resolves a natural implication question among classical weak-choice principles: BPI, even together with DC, need not provide a Hamel basis of R. Because BPI implies Hahn--Banach, the same model also separates Hahn--Banach from the real Hamel-basis assertion. This is structurally meaningful foundational information, not a routine reformulation.
